data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'd-j-l' meaning 'to guide, to help'. The name Djillali signifies a righteous and wise leader who guides and helps others. The name Djillali carries the meaning “Guide, Helper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Djillali usually hope their child will grow to embody guide, helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_arabic.name: جلالي
in_arabic.meaning: المعنى: اسم عربي يرمز إلى الكرم والجلال والكرمة الإلهية.
in_arabic.long_meaning: المعنى: الجلالي اسم عربي يعني الكرم والجلال والكرمة الإلهية، وهو اسم يرمز إلى الصفات الإلهية العظيمة. يأتي هذا الاسم من الجلال، الذي هو مصدر الكرم والجلال. في الإسلام، يرمز الجلال إلى الكرمة الإلهية والجلال والسماحة. يعتبر هذا الاسم اسمًا فخمًا ومتنوعًا، ويتمتع بخاصية العلاقة بالله، حيث يرمز إلى ارتباط الفرد بالله. في القرآن الكريم، يشار إلى الله بالجلال، مما يعطي هذا الاسم أهمية كبيرة في الإسلام. يُعتبر الجلالي اسمًا رائعًا للفتيات والذكور، حيث يعكس الجلال والكرمة الإلهية.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun describes the Almoravid ruler, Djillali ibn Yasin (1052-1106 CE) as the founder of the Almoravid Empire in the Maghreb.
historical_references.context: The Almoravids were a Berber dynasty that ruled much of the Maghreb and Al-Andalus from 1052 to 1147 CE. Djillali ibn Yasin, also known as Djillali Ben Rashid, was an influential Sufi leader who unified the Berber tribes under his rule and expanded the empire to include parts of modern-day Mauritania, Mali, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, and Spain.

historical_references.reference: Al-Biruni mentions Djillali ibn Abd al-Asad (980-1048 CE), a Persian scholar and astronomer, as the founder of the observatory at Ghazni.
historical_references.context: Al-Biruni was a prominent Persian scholar, scientist, and philosopher who wrote extensively on various subjects, including mathematics, astronomy, and geography. Djillali ibn Abd al-Asad, also known as Djillali al-Bharuni, was a Persian astronomer who is believed to have founded the observatory at Ghazni in modern-day Afghanistan, which was used to study the celestial bodies and make astronomical observations.
